headline: Computational models prioritize antibacterial drugs, dual targets and treatments
label: Computational Antibacterial Drug Prediction
summary: Mechanistic and learned models now yield decision-level outputs, from target-pair selection to clinical treatment guidance.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of antibacterial agents and treatments from explicit mechanistic or learned representations of drug and pathogen. A kinetic model of the E. coli folate pathway ranks DHPS and DHFR as a synergistic dual-target pair, with sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim used for validation. A graph neural network ensemble for Acinetobacter baumannii predicts antibacterial activity from atom features alone, and its explainability analysis highlights piperazine. SensiTyper converts whole-genome sequencing data into gonococcal antimicrobial susceptibility predictions that guide individualized treatment, tested on 13,701 genomes. The new element is translation toward decision-level outputs, including target-pair selection, candidate ranking, and clinical treatment guidance. The items do not share a single modeling framework, so the common thread is the output type rather than the method.
